content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Kathryn Bishop (E023) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory has two notes:
- Note 1: role Engineer, employment type full_time, recommends write for Payroll.
- Note 2: role Engineer, employment type contractor, security training basic, recommends read for Payroll. It says the Security DB shows contractor with basic training, not full-time as previously noted.

So the contradiction: one note says full-time, another says contractor. The second note says Security DB shows contractor. Hmm.

Access policy:
- full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns system. Payroll is owned by Payroll Specialist role; Engineer does not own it, so admin not allowed. Max = write.
- contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin. Since she has basic training, max = read.

Requested: write.

If full-time: max write, grant write.
If contractor with basic training: max read, grant read.

Which note to trust? The security note says "Security DB shows... contractor." The second note appears to be the more authoritative/recent correction. But which one is correct? The task gives us conflicting facts. Typically in these puzzles, the Security agent's note is the authoritative one (security training DB). The HR note said full-time, but security says contractor. The recommendation differs.

I think the correct decision is to follow the security note: contractor, basic training → max read. Requested write is above max, so grant read.

Let me submit read.
